fields.goal: Take the ArgentSea spec corpus from the outer quarter of the library to whole-surface coverage through a sequence of scoped Spec Populator runs, so the corpus can answer what is specified, what is specified but untested, and what the constitution promises but nothing implements.
fields.context:
## Where the corpus stands

111 blocks are committed: 8 Components, 17 Interfaces, 11 Schemas, 37 Behavioral/Scenario, 8 Invariants, 20 Terms, an 8-block constitution, and one reset Note sitting in the otherwise empty `adr` document. Ninety-four of those arrived from the 2026-08-11 Spec Populator run and were accepted after review.

That run's blocks are **individually excellent**: 94/94 carry structural `sources` (192 entries, 134 with line ranges), 70 references and 15 `illustrates` refs resolve with zero dangling, no block was misfiled, and eight spot-checked claims were all accurate against the code — including Npgsql `Prepare()` being skipped when the connection string contains `multiplexing=true`, the eight-asterisk password mask, and shard-id uniqueness being enforced by an `ImmutableDictionary` builder that throws.

**They are also collectively narrow.** 119 of 169 public types are never mentioned, and the gap is the middle of the library, not its edges.

## What is missing

- **The query-execution API — what every consumer actually calls — has one Interface block.** `QueryAsync`, `MapListAsync`, `MapReaderAsync`, `MapOutputAsync` (nine `TReaderResult0..7` arities), `ReturnValueAsync`, `ListAsync` and `RunAsync` across `ShardDataConnection`, `ShardSetReadAll`, `SqlDatabases`/`PgDatabases`: hundreds of public overloads, essentially unspecified.
- `ShardSetReadFirst` and `ShardSetWrite` are **entirely absent** — two of the three fan-out modes.
- **`ShardKey` round-trip behaviour has one Interface contract and no Behavioral, Scenario or Invariant** — the library's signature feature, and its most heavily tested area.
- The `MapTo*` families (23 SQL Server + 22 PostgreSQL attributes, `SqlParameterCollectionExtensions.cs` alone past 1,377 lines, plus the `SupportedTypes.md` matrix) are represented by **one** Schema block for Pg varchar. `MapShardKeyAttribute` and its two provider variants — the mechanism that hydrates a ShardKey from a row — are absent.
- DI registration (`SqlServiceBuilderExtensions`, `PgServiceBuilderExtensions`), how every consumer bootstraps: absent.
- 14 of 16 exception types: absent. Orleans: 37 files, 4 blocks.
- **Zero ADRs.** The `adr` document holds one corpus-reset Note and nothing else.

## The constitution is the yardstick, and it has holes

Measured against the eight committed constitution blocks: **P3 (stay a thin, composable layer over ADO.NET, with an escape hatch) has zero descriptive blocks.** P6's circuit breaker exists only as a glossary Term despite concrete, testable defaults in `DataConnectionManager` (20 failures, 5000 ms). P7's 'a single model class targets exactly one provider' is enforced by `MultipleMapAttributesException` and captured by no Invariant. P2's compiled-expression caching has one diagnostic-logging Behavioral but no invariant that the delegate is built once per model type. And **'tenant' — half the project's stated purpose under P1's tenant-isolation clause — is not even a glossary Term.**

## Why the coverage is inverted, and why that matters here

The best-tested areas of the repository are the least specified. `ShardKeyRobustTests`, `ShardSerializationTests`, the mapping and configuration tests cover exactly what the corpus does not; meanwhile `DatabaseBatch`/`ShardSetBatch` result selection, `ShardsValues`, `ReadAll`, `GetIsErrorTransient` and `CopyMapper` are all specified and have **zero test files**. So today the corpus is a usable gap-finder but not a coverage baseline: an audit against it would report high conformance while touching a minority of the library. Closing these gaps is what turns it into a baseline.

## Shape of the campaign

Several cheap scoped runs, not one giant one. Each run is pointed at a named area, runs Phase 1 only, and lands pending proposals for curation. Runs are additive rather than duplicative because the apparatus reads the committed corpus first and amends instead of re-proposing.

**This brief is blocked on agentic `brief-27c7e068a996483bb49dc43360a7530a`.** Without U1 (brownfield census and adopt-don't-repropose) the Partition Planner re-proposes the eight Components already accepted and the coverage matrix reports all-`pending` as if nothing existed. Without U8 (optional run scoping) a run cannot be pointed at an area at all. U4 supplies the counted coverage fractions these acceptance criteria are stated in, and U7 (withdraw guard) is what lets a later run retire an earlier one's defective pending proposals — see the constraint about brief identity below.
constraints: BLOCKED on agentic brief-27c7e068a996483bb49dc43360a7530a. U1 (brownfield census) and U8 (run scoping) are hard prerequisites — without them a scoped run re-proposes the accepted corpus or cannot be scoped at all. U4 supplies the coverage fractions these criteria are written in.

U7's same-brief withdraw guard keys on the brief id stamped at propose time. If the scoped runs are dispatched as CHILD briefs of this campaign, each run stamps its own child id and a later run still cannot retire an earlier one's pending proposals. Either U7 must compare the campaign ROOT of the decomposition chain, or every run must be dispatched under this brief's id. Resolve this before the second run starts, or drain each run's proposal queue to acceptance/rejection before the next run touches the same area.

The eight accepted Component names are canonical subject strings: AttributeMapping, BatchQueryExecution, ConfigurationAndResilience, DataConnectionAndQuery, OrleansIntegration, PostgreSqlProvider, ShardKeysAndFanOut, SqlServerProvider. No run may propose a duplicate Component or coin a new subject string for an existing one.
No run may re-propose a claim already committed among the 111 blocks; refinements arrive as amendments.

Each scoped run stops at the Phase 1 gate. The normative corpus already exists as the eight-block constitution and must not be regenerated per-run — a per-run elicitation would fragment exactly what the single-merger design protects.
Every run stays read-only on the repository and lands PENDING proposals; nothing in this campaign commits spec truth without human curation.
Curate between runs. Accepting a block a skeptic left flagged holds its provenance at GeneratedProposal rather than promoting it, so the queue is worth reading rather than bulk-accepting.

deliverables.name: R1 - Query-execution API run
deliverables.description: Scope: the query-execution surface — ShardDataConnection, ShardSetReadAll, ShardSetReadFirst, ShardSetWrite, ShardSetsBase, ShardInstance, DatabasesBase, SqlDatabases, PgDatabases, SimpleDbConnection, IDataConnection, DataConnectionManager's execution path, QueryResultModelHandler, and the Query/QueryProcedure/QueryStatement trio's interaction with them. Owning Components: DataConnectionAndQuery and ShardKeysAndFanOut. This is the largest and highest-value gap: the API every consumer calls, presently one Interface block. Expect method-family compression to carry the weight — one Interface per family (name plus semantics) whose contract states the overload dimensions: optional shardParameterName, optional TArg pass-through, the ShardsValues subset variant, and the TReaderResult0..7 arities mapping result sets in declaration order. Run first: its vocabulary is the most central, so the amendments it makes to the committed glossary set the baseline the later runs extend.

deliverables.name: R2 - ShardKey identity and serialization run
deliverables.description: Scope: ShardKey<TRecord> and ShardKey<TRecord,TChild>, ShardChild, ShardGrandChild, ShardGreatGrandChild, GhostShardKey, IKeyedModel, IShardKey, ShardKeySerialization, and the external-string helpers in StringExtensions. Owning Component: ShardKeysAndFanOut. The library's signature feature and its most heavily tested area, currently holding one Interface contract and nothing behavioural. Priorities: external-string and binary round-trip (ToExternalString/FromExternalString, ToArray, ToUtf8, TryParse), equality and the Empty sentinel, the shard-id/record-id/type-metadata composition and what makes metadata invalid, and the hierarchy's parent-child key derivation. Because ShardKeyRobustTests and ShardSerializationTests already exercise this area heavily, the run should read the tests as a source alongside the code — and the resulting blocks are what finally make the existing test suite auditable against a spec.

deliverables.name: R3 - Mapping attribute families and the type matrix run
deliverables.description: Scope: the 23 MapToSql* and 22 MapToPg* attributes, SqlParameterCollectionExtensions and PgParameterCollectionExtensions, SqlParameterExtensions and PgParameterExtensions, ParameterMapAttributeBase, SqlParameterMapAttribute and PgParameterMapAttribute, MapShardKeyAttribute with MapSqlShardKeyAttribute and MapPgShardKeyAttribute, MapToModel, ExpressionHelpers, the Mapper's cache and delegate-compilation path, and the SupportedTypes.md matrix. Owning Components: AttributeMapping, SqlServerProvider, PostgreSqlProvider. This is the single largest body of code in the library and is currently one Schema block. Family compression is mandatory here: one Schema block per attribute family with the type matrix as members, plus the shard-key hydration Interface and the P2 invariant that the compiled delegate is built once per model type. The one-model-one-provider rule enforced by MultipleMapAttributesException belongs here as an Invariant.

deliverables.name: R4 - Configuration, DI and resilience run
deliverables.description: Scope: SqlServiceBuilderExtensions and PgServiceBuilderExtensions, SqlGlobalPropertiesOptions and PgGlobalPropertiesOptions, the Sql/Pg connection and shard-connection options and their Configuration counterparts, SqlConnectionPropertiesBase and PgConnectionPropertiesBase, DataConnectionConfigurationBase, DataConnectionManager's Polly policy construction, SequenceLengthening, RetryLimitExceededException, and LoggingExtensions with its event identifiers. Owning Component: ConfigurationAndResilience. Two named gaps to close: the bootstrap path every consumer uses is unspecified, and circuit breaking exists only as a glossary Term despite concrete testable defaults (20 failures, 5000 ms) in DataConnectionManager. The hereditary configuration hierarchy already has a good Behavioral — extend it rather than restating it. Note that RetryLimitExceededException was found declared but never thrown: confirm before speccing, and route it to open-questions as unreachable declared surface if that still holds.

deliverables.name: R5 - Orleans integration run
deliverables.description: Scope: the whole of ArgentSea.Orleans and ArgentSea.Orleans.Sql — ArgentSeaDbGrainPersistence and ArgentSeaShardGrainPersistence, the two options validators and their options types, OrleansQueryDefinitions with QueryResultFormat, IdParser, SpanParser, OrleansExpressionHelper, ShardKeyOrleansSerializer, FakeGrainStorageSerializer, the clustering provider builder with ArgentSeaGatewayListProvider and ArgentSeaOrleansMembershipTable, the reminder table and its provider builder, ArgentSeaGrainStorageFactory and the silo builder extensions, the five Orleans exception types, and common.sql with tenant.sql. Owning Component: OrleansIntegration. Thirty-seven source files presently covered by four blocks. Priorities: grain state read/write/clear including ETag concurrency, grain identity parsing and its failure modes, and the SQL schema contracts the providers depend on.

deliverables.name: R6 - Consolidation: ADRs, exception taxonomy and constitution closure
deliverables.description: The campaign's closing run, and the single owner of what the area runs must not fragment. Three jobs. FIRST, ADRs: the adr document holds one reset Note and no decisions — record the as-built choices from git history and the DocFx design docs (attribute mapping over convention, stored-procedure-first, compiled expression trees over per-call reflection, the ShardKey binary layout, one-model-one-provider, Polly for resilience, and the netstandard2.0/2.1 plus net8/net9 multi-target set). SECOND, the exception taxonomy as a cross-cutting claim set: 16 types across the shared core and Orleans, of which two are covered; each throw-reachable type becomes the rejection path of a Behavioral, and any declared-but-never-raised type goes to open-questions instead. THIRD, constitution closure: run the alignment table over the finished corpus and close what the area runs left — P3's thin-layer and escape-hatch promise, which no run naturally owns, and the tenant-isolation vocabulary that P1 names and the glossary lacks. Run last, when every area run's proposals are curated, so its table reflects the finished corpus.
